findings.claim: Across the observed score window [0.0,0.49] the landmark_00_local_dx curve is non-monotone: it rises to a positive peak near t≈0.10-0.11, falls to a negative trough near t≈0.19, then recovers toward baseline by t≈0.49; the whole-window mean is near zero (whole_window_z≈-0.18) with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches.

landmark_00_local_dy shows an early negative excursion (values_z≈-1.0 to -1.3 over t≈0.02-0.09) followed by a return toward zero and a mildly positive late window; whole-window mean is slightly negative (whole_window_z≈-0.30), 6 sign changes, 4 strong sign conflicts.

landmark_00_local_dz is near zero early, becomes positive over roughly t≈0.04-0.42, and turns negative in the last few nodes (last_z≈-0.59); whole-window mean is essentially zero (whole_window_z≈-0.02) with 10 sign changes and 7 strong sign conflicts, so no stable signed level is established.

landmark_00_soft_mass is the most coherent of the read features: it rises from negative early values to a positive plateau (values_z≈1.0-1.6) over roughly t≈0.14-0.30, then decays to slightly negative by t≈0.49; whole-window mean is positive (whole_window_z≈0.64) with only 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict.

landmark_01_local_dx and landmark_01_local_dz both show an early negative dip (t≈0.02-0.09) followed by a positive excursion peaking near t≈0.14-0.18 and a return toward baseline; whole-window means are near zero (whole_window_z≈-0.22 and -0.01 respectively) with 4-6 sign changes and 5-10 strong sign conflicts.

landmark_01_local_dy is persistently negative over most of the window (values_z≈-0.3 to -1.2) with only a late approach to zero; whole-window mean is negative (whole_window_z≈-0.50), 4 sign changes, 4 strong sign conflicts.

landmark_01_soft_mass rises from a positive early value through a negative mid-window dip (t≈0.04-0.09) and recovers to positive late values; whole-window mean is slightly negative (whole_window_z≈-0.25) with 4 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts.

The score clock is a uniform 50-node grid over [0.0,0.49] with learning_window [0.0,0.5] and label semantics 'Recorded affinities removed; equal score prior'; no decoded affinity labels are present, so these curves are coordinate observables only and carry no measured affinity or survival outcome.

hypotheses.direction: increase mid-window soft_mass relative to the early and late window
hypotheses.falsifier: If the mid-window soft_mass excursion does not change under the registered curvature schedule, or if the whole-window mean and sign-change count are unchanged, the observed contrast is not controllable by this coordinate reward.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass (predicted endpoint world A, z-scored per node)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate exhibits a single broad positive excursion over the middle of the observed window (rise from negative early values, plateau near t≈0.14-0.30, decay to slightly negative by t≈0.49). A reward schedule that applies its larger curvature (delta) during the mid-window rise/plateau and baseline curvature at the endpoints would test whether the observed mid-window mass excursion is a controllable contrast rather than a stationary target.

hypotheses.direction: reduce the early negative dx/dy excursion toward zero
hypotheses.falsifier: If the early-window dx/dy values remain at their observed negative levels under the registered schedule, or if the sign-change count and strong-sign-conflict count are unchanged, the early contrast is not being controlled.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy (predicted endpoint world A, z-scored per node)
hypotheses.scope: regional, early window t≈0.0-0.15 within the observed support
hypotheses.statement: landmark_00_local_dx and landmark_00_local_dy both show an early-window negative excursion (t≈0.02-0.09) that reverses sign by mid-window. A schedule that applies larger curvature early and relaxes to baseline later would test whether the early negative dx/dy excursion is a reproducible early-window contrast rather than a stationary offset.

hypotheses.direction: raise landmark_01_local_dy toward zero over the sustained negative region
hypotheses.falsifier: If landmark_01_local_dy remains persistently negative with the same whole-window mean and sign-change count under the registered schedule, the sustained contrast is not controllable by this coordinate reward.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_01_local_dy (predicted endpoint world A, z-scored per node)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: landmark_01_local_dy is persistently negative across most of the observed window with only a late approach to zero, unlike the sign-reversing landmark_00 dx/dy curves. A schedule that applies larger curvature over the sustained negative region would test whether this sustained negative dy is a stable coordinate contrast that can be shifted, rather than a stationary target.

limitations: Only 8 of 200 catalogue curve features were read (landmark_00 and landmark_01 dx/dy/dz/soft_mass); the remaining 192 features, including all local_cxx/cxy/cxz/cyy/cyz/czz components and landmarks 02-19, are unqueried and are not evidence of absence or of any direction.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available; all statements rest on the continuous per-node curves only.

All read curves have polynomial_accepted=false and relative_node_RMSE between ~0.29 and ~0.78, with 4-10 sign changes and 1-10 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so no stable signed level or monotone trend is established for any read feature.

The score clock metadata states recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior is used; no decoded final affinity, survival, or last recorded joint-head score is available, so none of these coordinate contrasts is evidence of descendant survival or measured final benefit.
These are coordinate observables in predicted endpoint world A; no energy, chemical-interaction, or neural-module interpretation is attached to them.
Time derivatives of these curves are not spatial reward gradients and do not estimate an optimal guidance dose; no absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient is inferred here.

evidence_delivery.Analyst: Declare curve_features for every hypothesis; read get_curve/get_curves, then cite a matching delivered handle for every declared feature. Summaries are not curves. Keep unsupported observations in findings/limitations, not actionable hypotheses.
evidence_delivery.Designer: For each adopted hypothesis and each of its features, cite the actual inherited curve/profile handle. Only registered choices; retaining M2 is allowed.
